solutions.check: 27 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Industrial action has greedy western leaders appropriating capital

indicators.note: to appropriate is to take something into your possession, so the outer letters take in another piece
leaders go at the front, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words
the capital city of Norway

explanation.surface: A strike is blamed on greedy Western bosses grabbing the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money in the surface, but it is a capital city. 'leaders' picks the first letters of 'greedy western', which then wrap round the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is a protest where workers deliberately reduce output, a recognised form of strike action.

clue.text: Acts in accordance with Fish, taking drugs

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a goby is a small fish
E is ecstasy, so more than one is ES

explanation.surface: Someone follows the instructions of a man named Fish while on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F makes 'Fish' look like a person's name; it is just a fish. E as ecstasy is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by rules or advice is an idiom for following them or being guided by them.

clue.text: Pain and grief's fun, in an odd way

indicators.note: doing something in an odd way means not in the usual order, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter, including the S of the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A wry remark that pain and grief can be strangely enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'grief's' is part of the letters to rearrange, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffering is a noun meaning the state of enduring physical or emotional distress, a close synonym.

clue.text: The place to make a film, 'Storming'

definitions.text: The place to make a film
definitions.meaning: first meaning: where filming happens, as two words
second meaning: an attack or assault, as one word

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Storming' look like a film title; it is a noun for an attack, matching the answer read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors work 'on set' in a studio, while an onset is an assault or attack, like storming a position.

clue.text: Balls, cut by very kinky love, developed?

indicators.note: something cut by an object has that object driven into it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Ed Balls is a former Labour cabinet minister turned broadcaster
V is the standard abbreviation for very

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent out of the normal shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether kinky sex has made someone mature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' is the surname of politician Ed Balls, so it gives his first name; V plus the rearranged word go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolved is a past participle meaning grown or changed gradually, matching developed in sense and form.

clue.text: Zeal is a feature of destructive he-men, certainly

indicators.note: a feature of something is part of it, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Macho men smashing things up are certainly full of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from destructiVE HE-MEN CErtainly, ignoring the hyphen and comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehemence is forceful passion or intensity of feeling, close in meaning to fervour or ardour.

clue.text: Fly comes undone, going round each green

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other
something that comes undone falls apart from its tidy order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
EA is the usual abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Someone's trouser zip comes open while walking round a golf green.
explanation.walkthrough: The fly here sounds like a trouser zip, but it is just three letters to rearrange; 'green' is the definition, not a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy place is full of foliage and trees, so it looks verdant and lush.

clue.text: Finally, Conservative member gets cane out, showing refinement

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this word

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory MP produces a cane, an old-school sign of good breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a Member of Parliament but is a body part, the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is grace and polish in manner or style, a direct synonym for this kind of sophistication.

clue.text: Gunboat diplomacy? "Low prospect," I repeated, "for change"

indicators.note: these letters are offered up to be changed, that is reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter
the letter I given twice

explanation.surface: A politician gloomily admits that bullying abroad is unlikely to bring change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' is not a separate device: it doubles the I to complete the thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunboat diplomacy, threatening force to get your way, is one example of international dealings driven by military might, hence the question mark.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Trump-like, though personally not having taken an extreme position?

parts.note: surface reading: an egotist like Donald Trump

parts.words: though personally not having taken an extreme position
parts.note: setter's reading: the person sits in the middle, not at either extreme, a centrist

explanation.surface: A jibe that Trump is all about himself, though not politically extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer literally: oneself placed in the centre, a moderate rather than an extremist, which is ironic for Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotistic people preoccupied with their own interests are described with this word, which fits the popular image of Trump.

clue.text: Sibyl's so-so earthy broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A woman called Sibyl has a mediocre, down-to-earth radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: Sibyl looks like a first name, as in Fawlty Towers, but a sibyl is a prophetess of ancient legend; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a woman of classical antiquity believed to utter prophecies, so she foretells the future.

clue.text: A bishop 'delivered' by drug (twice) — he's at another place

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
something delivered has been sent
E is ecstasy, given twice; 'by' just places it next

explanation.surface: A clergyman is dosed up, and his mind is elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another place' is also the Commons' coy phrase for the House of Lords, where bishops sit; here it simply means somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone missing from where they should be, so they are elsewhere instead.

clue.text: Ex-PM pitched against ex-political broadcaster — call for help!

parts.note: Theresa May, former UK Prime Minister
Sir Robin Day, the late BBC political interviewer

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister faces a grilling from a veteran interviewer and pleads for rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Day was a famously combative British TV political interviewer; 'pitched against' only sets the two names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayday is the international radio distress signal used by ships and aircraft in grave danger.

clue.text: Elected Democrat: "Need Pence to break up liberty"

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: breaking something up smashes its order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A newly elected Democrat says Mike Pence must be stopped to save American freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: Pence is Mike Pence, Trump's Vice-President, but here just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence is freedom from outside control, a synonym for liberty in the political sense.

clue.text: To belittle and head off Biden's reform, strike a false note

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the top, so the first letter is dropped
to reform is to form again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the president's surname without its first letter
to grate is to make a harsh, jarring sound

explanation.surface: A critic says that mocking Biden's reforms sounds a wrong note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' looks like a policy noun in the surface, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to disparage or criticise unfairly, making someone seem unimportant.

clue.text: With intervention of the body politic, career is set back — it could get a whole family on the move

definitions.text: it could get a whole family on the move

indicators.note: something that intervenes comes between, so one piece is placed in the middle of another
set back means moved backwards, so these letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: to career is to rush along, to race
the state is the nation as an organised political body

explanation.surface: A politician's career stalls when the government steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' reads as a noun for someone's working life; it is a verb meaning to rush. An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A station wagon has a long rear load space and room for passengers, so it suits carrying a household with luggage.

clue.text: A medicinal sweet from Dicky, covered in mush

indicators.note: something covered in a substance is wrapped by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a paste is a soft, mushy mixture
dicky is British slang for unwell or unsound, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: A cough sweet comes from someone called Dicky, smothered in goo.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D makes 'Dicky' look like a name; it is the British informal adjective for poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small lozenge, often sucked to soothe a sore throat, so it is a sweet with healing use.

clue.text: On the outside an arse, not one to be taken lightly

definitions.text: not one to be taken lightly

parts.note: on the margin, at the edge
seat is a polite word for the backside

explanation.surface: A rude jibe about someone being an outsider and a fool who must be watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arse' looks like an insult but means the backside. In Britain a marginal seat is a parliamentary constituency held by a small majority.
explanation.definitionFit: Constituencies won by narrow majorities can easily change hands at an election, so parties never treat them casually.

clue.text: Feeling tense, love — need to be stimulated around top of genitals

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped about another
stimulating something stirs it up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A bawdy picture of someone aroused and frustrated, waiting for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters wrap round the single G, and the tennis O goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on edge is an idiom for being nervous, anxious or irritable.

clue.text: Firm Melody squeezing T Rex

indicators.note: squeezing something means holding it tightly within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a song is a melody
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone named Melody hugs a dinosaur, or the glam rock band T. Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: T. Rex was a 1970s glam rock band, which makes 'Melody' look musical; R for rex (king) is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and strong both describe something solid, robust and hard to break.

clue.text: Should get tough pissed

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunk things lurch out of order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice that a drunk ought to be dealt with firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang pissed means drunk, not angry as in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are modal verbs expressing obligation or duty, as in 'you should go' and 'you ought to go'.

clue.text: Seductive politician can get mad on the outside

indicators.note: being on the outside means surrounding, so one piece encloses another
mad means crazed and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a tin is a can
taken as written
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An alluring politician who can become furious and look unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can get' looks like 'is able to become'; it is two pieces of fodder, a tin and the word get.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tempting is alluring and hard to resist, an adjective just like seductive.

clue.text: (& 24ac.) Flashy system buggered up some credo?

indicators.note: buggered up is British slang for ruined or messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A showy belief system has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flashy' looks like showy, but it means sent by flashes of light, as signal lamps do.
explanation.definitionFit: This dots-and-dashes signalling method can be transmitted by flashing a lamp as well as by sound or radio.

clue.text: Choke Santa's reindeer, one making a clatter

parts.note: to clog is to block or choke up
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A violent instruction to throttle one of Santa's reindeer, which then clatters about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choke' sounds like strangling, but it means block up.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog dancer stamps out rhythms in wooden-soled shoes, producing a loud rattling noise on the floor.

Democratic experiment starts with a Native American order
